power.why: AEP has stated it does not have sufficient transmission capacity to serve all planned buildings on this campus, a regional constraint rather than a site one.
power.duration: AEP holds a six-year agreement with Bloom Energy; the fuel cells are expected to run only until transmission capacity is available.
power.gas_supply: A separate 8-inch intrastate pipeline, route not yet final; at nine inches or under serving a single customer it needs no pre-installation approval from the Ohio Power Siting Board or PUCO.
power.technology: Solid oxide fuel cells. Natural gas reacts with steam and air to produce hydrogen and carbon dioxide, generating electricity electrochemically rather than by combustion.

profile.campus: Amazon Scioto Darby Creek Road campus, Hilliard, Ohio (142 acres)
profile.address: Scioto Darby Road, Hilliard, Norwich Township, Franklin County, Ohio, 43026
profile.reading:
This building is one of the data center structures Amazon Web Services operates around New Albany, Ohio, a Columbus suburb spanning Franklin, Licking, and Union counties, the physical location of AWS's US-EAST-2 cloud region.

AWS's Ohio buildout has been documented in stages by the company, the City of New Albany, and Ohio trade and local press. The City of New Albany reported in August 2025 that AWS's cumulative capital investment in the area had reached $6.2 billion since 2015, that AWS had invested $19.7 billion across Ohio over that period, and that AWS operations in New Albany had contributed $1.4 billion to Licking County gross domestic product; the city's release also cited a further $10 billion in Ohio expansion AWS announced in 2024 and a forecast $23 billion cumulative investment by 2030. In August 2023, New Albany City Council approved a further $3.5 billion AWS investment covering five additional data center buildings, according to 10TV and Data Center Frontier coverage of that council vote. CoStar separately reported in 2024 that AWS's disclosed Ohio data center investment had grown by a further $10 billion. The City of New Albany's 2025 release stated AWS had completed and staffed two data center buildings in the area, with additional facilities under construction and expected to become operational later that year, and that AWS-related activity supported an estimated 1,550 full time equivalent jobs annually in Licking County and paid $3.1 million in property taxes and fees to the county in 2024.

AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or IT power rating for this individual building, and none of the city, county, or trade press coverage found for this page breaks the New Albany campus down building by building. This structure is treated as part of the documented AWS Ohio footprint described above.

profile.capacity_note: The 72.9 MW figure is ON-SITE GENERATION, not IT load. It is the fuel cell plant AEP Ohio is building to serve this campus behind the meter; Amazon publishes no IT capacity figure for any building here, and the two numbers are not interchangeable.
profile.facility_note: AWS has not identified this specific building by name, construction date, or operational status in any source found for this page. The City of New Albany's August 2025 release states two of the campus buildings were complete and staffed and others remained under construction; which category this particular structure falls into is not independently confirmed.
profile.research_note: Reading written 2026-09-03 by srj-thinpage-writer session (Sonnet). Verified via fresh web search/fetch this session (not reused from 2026-09-02 batch without re-checking): AWS aboutamazon.com investment pages, state/city economic development releases, and named trade/local press, listed in sources. AWS does not publish a per-building street address, opening date, square footage, or IT power rating for this structure; none of the sources checked break the named campus down building by building. Prior batch's disclosure_policy claim (citing aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/ as directly confirming a non-disclosure policy) was checked directly this session and found to be overstated -- that page does not discuss facility-level disclosure at all -- so it was not reused verbatim; the non-disclosure finding here rests instead on the absence of building-level figures across every source checked, consistent with trade-press characterization of AWS's practice.
profile.community_note: Hilliard asked AEP and Bloom Energy to add carbon capture, citing CO2 volume and resident health. Modelling commissioned by the city and published February 2026 found the plant would raise CO2 by about 27.7 ppm at the nearest home 800 feet away and about 3.6 ppm at Beacon Elementary School 4,000 feet away, against an ambient 350 to 450 ppm and a health threshold generally taken to begin near 5,000 ppm. A second independent study in May 2026 confirmed the method. Ohio EPA did not set a CO2 limit in the air permit because other regulated pollutants fall below federal thresholds.
profile.incentives_note: A Community Reinvestment Act agreement with Hilliard abates property tax on data centre buildings against a $200 million investment by 31 December 2026, which the city states Amazon has met or exceeded. Hilliard City School District receives up to $3.4 million a year: $400,000 plus $1.50 per square foot of building, against up to two million square feet planned.
profile.regulatory_note: The plant is exempt from Hilliard zoning: Ohio Revised Code 4906.13(B) gives the Ohio Power Siting Board exclusive jurisdiction over generation above 50 MW, and no local government may permit or condition a facility holding an OPSB certificate.
profile.regional_context: New Albany, a Columbus, Ohio suburb, has become one of the Midwest's fastest growing data center markets since AWS selected the area for its Ohio cloud region in the mid-2010s. American Electric Power's Ohio utility serves the corridor and has filed with state regulators over large-load data center interconnection requests as the New Albany, Licking County, and Union County buildout has expanded. Ohio offers a data center sales and use tax exemption administered by the state Development Services Agency, tied to minimum investment and payroll commitments, which local officials and trade press credit with drawing AWS and other operators to the corridor. New Albany markets itself alongside Intel's nearby semiconductor investment in Licking County as part of a broader technology corridor sometimes called the Silicon Heartland, and hosts data center campuses for other operators including Meta and Google in addition to AWS. Local governments in New Albany, Licking County, and Union County have negotiated a series of tax abatement and community benefit agreements with AWS, documented in city council minutes and covered by 10TV and Data Center Frontier.
profile.onsite_generation_type: solid oxide fuel cell, 228 Bloom Energy units, natural gas
profile.onsite_generation_owner: Ohio Power Company (AEP Ohio), behind the meter, no grid export
profile.onsite_generation_status: Approved by the Ohio Power Siting Board 2025-09-22; construction from January 2026; projected operational September 2027

reading.body:
AWS does not publish an IT power capacity for this building. AEP Ohio is building a 72.9 MW solid oxide fuel cell plant behind the meter, scheduled operational September 2027, which will serve this structure and others on the 142-acre Scioto Darby Creek campus. This is on-site generation, not IT load. The fuel cells will run on natural gas through a dedicated 8-inch pipeline until AEP acquires sufficient transmission capacity to serve all planned campus buildings, a regional grid constraint. AEP holds a six-year agreement with Bloom Energy to operate the 228 fuel cell units; the plant is exempt from local zoning under Ohio state law.

The 72.9 MW generation capacity cannot be directly translated to rack or accelerator count without knowing the campus's actual IT load, which AWS has not disclosed. If the entire output served AI training at a common 40 kW per rack, the math would suggest roughly 1,820 racks, but this assumes a specific utilization and load profile AWS has not confirmed. The fuel cells produce roughly 1.45 million pounds of CO2 per day. Two independent air dispersion studies commissioned by Hilliard in 2026 found the plant would raise local CO2 by 27.7 ppm at the nearest home and 3.6 ppm at the nearest school, below health thresholds and federal regulatory limits.

This campus is part of AWS's documented $6.2 billion Ohio investment since 2015, concentrated in the New Albany and Hilliard corridor as part of the US-EAST-2 cloud region. The City of New Albany reported in August 2025 that AWS had completed and staffed two campus buildings with others under construction. Ohio has 77 mapped data center facilities of which only 8 have published megawatt figures totaling 60.4 MW; this fuel cell plant alone, if matched by comparable IT loads across the region, would materially increase Ohio's published capacity. The campus operating status and IT load remain unconfirmed by AWS.
